answer: The horizon detector writes to vault, and ledge makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 41 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 269 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
